subject: [hw] DEC04: larb5 IS written by the vendor (0x1600d00c sleep-protect), so "larb read-only" needs the allow-list; VDEC_ALL covers every listed frame address
body:
Evidence from opus-dec1 (board, "get_ringbuf SOLVED"): during frame START the vendor does the larb5 sleep-protect handshake at 0x1600d00c: write bit 0, then poll bit 16 (vdec_hal_wait_larb_sleep_protect), and programs ~60 registers outside the frozen windows: 0x16011800..0x16013fff, 0x16016xxx, 0x16002004/0x1600201c. On the real tree that produced 50000 bad MMIOs; with the DEC04 window it should be zero.

Three consequences, please decide/confirm:

1) larb policy (hw-lead, DEC07, K02). The vendor WRITES larb5 0x1600d000+0xc; a flat "larb pages read-only" rule in the kernel would EACCES the sleep-protect handshake and could hang the frame (the library polls the ack 50000 times). The allow-list DEC07 mentioned needs at least larb5 offset 0x00c (write of bit 0, read/poll of bit 16). larb4 0x1602e000: no write seen yet in this trace; keep read-only until DEC02 shows one. Proposed text for redwood_vcodec.h rev 3 comment / kernel rule: VDEC_ALL pages 0x0d000 and 0x2e000 are writable only at offsets the vendor uses for sleep protect (start with 0x00c on larb5), everything else read-only; unknown offsets are logged and refused, not silently allowed. If you prefer "whole larb page writable for now, tighten after DEC02", say so; the V40 model does not police it either way (it maps the page to VDEC_ALL and mmio_bad stays 0).

2) Window coverage (hw-lead, DEC07): every address opus-dec1 listed is inside 0x16000000+0x30000 and outside the ten old windows, i.e. exactly what RWVC_WIN_VDEC_ALL is for: 0x11800-0x13fff and 0x16xxx are pages 0x11/0x12/0x13/0x16, 0x2004/0x201c is page 0x2, larb5 0xd000 is page 0xd. The model side is ready (dec04.patch for V40); DEC02s trace should now show mmio_bad 0 for a frame instead of 50000.

3) DEC02: if your harness runs the frame with the patched model, please record mmio_reads/writes, mmio_bad (expect 0) and last_bad_mmio_addr, plus the per-page R/W split, and whether larb4 is touched at all. That page list is exactly what the kernel allow-list should shrink to.

Also, unrelated but for FACTS (hw-d01): opus-dec1 says VDEC_PROTOCOL.md 2.2 is wrong because VIDEO_MAX_FRAME=64, not 32: list_free_bs @0, list_free @0x210, list_disp @0xe20, dec @0x1a30, pic @0x1af8, vdec_bs_va @0x1ac8. I have not verified it myself; passing it on as [V] from opus-dec1 with the vendor addresses cited there.
